page: Microsoft Azure E4-2as_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 x86_64 processor clocked at 3.525 GHz. It provisions 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core across 2 hardware threads, backed by 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. It features 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a high ratio of 16.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. No dedicated GPUs or local storage drives are bundled with the instance, requiring network-attached storage such as Azure Premium Storage for persistence, and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default.

Performance benchmarks reflect the constrained compute footprint paired with high memory density. Single-threaded evaluation shows solid execution efficiency, highlighted by a stress-ng single-core score of 2699.28 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1499.0. However, multi-core throughput is constrained by the two-vCPU allocation, yielding a multi-core stress-ng metric of 2699.28 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 1883.0. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth measures 28.26 GB/s and write throughput achieves 20.87 GB/s. Application tests record Redis SET operations at 1.97 million ops/sec and static web serving throughput at 2.44 GB/s. Small model LLM text generation reaches 75.84 tokens per second, though prompt processing is limited to 126.69 tokens per second.

From a resource perspective, the E4-2as_v5 offers an economical entry into memory-intensive computing without the overhead of licensing large core counts. Because it pairs an ample 32.0 GB memory footprint with only two virtual threads, it provides a cost-effective design for memory-hungry services that do not demand parallel processing power. The primary tradeoff lies in raw computing throughput and the absence of integrated local NVMe storage, meaning disk-bound operations rely strictly on external block volumes. This server configuration fits small-to-medium in-memory caches, lightweight database servers, basic enterprise applications requiring large memory reserves, and single-threaded data manipulation tasks.

Configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs spanning a single physical core with two threads, the instance features an expansive 32.0 GB of RAM, yielding an elevated 16.0 GB per vCPU ratio. No local storage or discrete GPUs are integrated into the profile, necessitating remote block storage solutions such as Azure Premium Storage. Benchmark results demonstrate capable single-core execution with an average single-core Geekbench score of 1499.0 and a strong single-core stress-ng result, while multi-core workloads, memory throughput, and database operational metrics are naturally constrained by the dual-thread ceiling. This configuration delivers an efficient memory-to-vCPU allocation, making it appropriate for memory-bound workloads with low parallel processing demands, such as lightweight in-memory caching layers, modest transactional databases, and specialized enterprise services requiring significant memory headroom.
